title: Equilateral Sets in ℓₚⁿ Beyond n + 1: Linear Excess and Dimension Cost
content: How many equilateral points can ℓₚⁿ contain beyond n + 1? For every fixed real p > 4, we construct equilateral sets for which the number of points beyond n + 1 grows at least linearly with n. For every fixed dimension, we prove that the maximum is n + 1 at all sufficiently large finite p, with an explicit threshold. The least dimension admitting any fixed number of extra points is p¹⁺ᵒ⁽¹⁾ as p → ∞. The constructions and finite bounds are formalised in Lean. Thus p = 4 marks the boundary: n + 1 is exact in every dimension for 2 ≤ p ≤ 4, while at every fixed finite p > 4 the excess grows at least linearly with dimension.
